issues.description: DIRECT_MONOTONIC_BLOCK_SHIFT duplicated rather than imported from its source of truth.
issues.detail: The constant was previously imported from Lucene99FlatVectorsFormat; the move introduces a fresh copy on Lucene99ScalarQuantizedVectorsFormat. Two names now point at the same value with no compiler-enforced link. That is incidental complexity from the package split. Either re-import the original or document that the legacy format intentionally froze its own copy.

issues.description: fieldsWriter throws UnsupportedOperationException, complecting format identity with write capability.
issues.detail: A KnnVectorsFormat is now a value that sometimes can write and sometimes cannot, decided at call time by an exception. Read-only-ness is an essential property of a legacy codec; encode it in the type (a ReadOnlyKnnVectorsFormat base or sealed reader-only variant) rather than as a runtime trap. Otherwise every caller has to know the secret rule.

issues.description: Constructor still accepts numMergeWorkers and mergeExec that the read-only format silently discards.
issues.detail: The fields were removed but the constructor signature still takes numMergeWorkers, mergeExec, and validates them. Callers are passing data that has no effect, which complects the public API shape with the now-vestigial write path. A read-only format's value is (maxConn, beamWidth, bits, compress, confidenceInterval); the rest is dead input that misleads readers.

issues.description: Protected fields demoted to package-private encode an inheritance assumption that test subclasses live in the same package.
issues.detail: OffHeapQuantizedByteVectorValues and Lucene99ScalarQuantizedVectorsFormat fields went from protected to package-private. That works only because the RW test shims sit in the same package — a place-oriented coupling. If anyone moves the tests, the access breaks silently at compile time. Worth a comment naming the constraint or keeping protected where extension is the documented contract.

issues.description: The question that should have been asked first: what is the value of a 'legacy format that cannot write'?
issues.detail: The codec is being split into a read-only public artifact and a write-capable test-only subclass. That is a reasonable shape, but it means the production class is half a thing. Consider naming the read-only role explicitly in the type hierarchy (ReadOnlyKnnVectorsFormat) so the value of each class is decomposable into one concept rather than 'format minus writer'.

review.summary: The move itself is the right direction — legacy formats belong in backward_codecs, and isolating the writer into a test-only RW shim is a clean decomposition. The remaining complecting is in the format class itself: a single type now means both "describes the on-disk layout" and "may or may not write," with the write capability hidden behind an UnsupportedOperationException and a constructor that still accepts merge-executor arguments it no longer uses. That is EASY-NOT-SIMPLE — the existing API shape was preserved at the cost of the type telling the truth. A ReadOnlyKnnVectorsFormat parent (or sealed read-only variant) would make value, identity, and capability separable. The duplicated DIRECT_MONOTONIC_BLOCK_SHIFT constant and the protected-to-package-private field demotion are smaller place-oriented couplings worth tightening.
